record.label: NASA Earth Observatory · NISAR images of Hubbard Glacier
record.finding: NISAR images from November 26 and December 8, 2025 show rock and ice debris on Hubbard Glacier after the December 6 earthquake.

limits: Terrain shadow, snow conditions and glacier movement can also change VV backscatter. The change map highlights backscatter differences across the radar footprint.
verification: Cross-check visible debris near Mount King George and McArthur Peak with the published NISAR pair.
Use a later matched pass or cloud-free optical image to check whether the mapped debris persists.

outlook.summary: Check mapped runouts and the flatter ice below steep slopes for persistent debris or new movement on future passes.
outlook.condition: A slope-failure probability needs repeated mapped failures, snow and weather observations, and local validation.

record.label: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio · NISAR eruption time series
record.finding: The published NISAR time series from December 2025 through August 2026 shows lava spreading east of Krasheninnikov's northern crater.

limits: Every selectable date is compared with the first displayed Sentinel-1 pass, which was acquired during the eruption. Snow, lava texture and terrain shadow affect radar brightness.
verification: Compare the eastern flow margin across repeat passes and check the NISAR time series.
Cross-check any new boundary with a published volcanic activity assessment or thermal observations.

outlook.summary: If effusion continues from the same vent, the active eastern flow margin is the first place to check for growth on the next matched pass.
outlook.condition: A flow-reach forecast needs current vent activity, effusion rate, a fine DEM and a validated flow model.

reference.label: NASA OPERA surface water
reference.legend: Blue marks mapped radar surface water on July 11. It includes existing water.

record.label: NASA Disasters · Central Texas floods
record.finding: NASA documented flash flooding in the Guadalupe River basin on July 4. The July 11 radar pass shows conditions a week after the flood.

limits: Backscatter varies with water, vegetation and surface roughness. The July 11 OPERA water layer is a dated observation and does not capture the July 4 peak flood extent.
verification: Use the Kerrville gauge record to check peak timing independently of the radar acquisitions.
Compare the mapped July 11 surface water with pre-event water, local imagery and documented high-water marks.

outlook.summary: Historical one-hour river-stage replay at the USGS Kerrville gauge.
outlook.condition: The model uses recent river stage. A forecast of where water spreads requires hydraulic modeling, rainfall forecasts and channel data.

reference.label: NASA NISAR displacement
reference.legend: Radar line-of-sight displacement: blue −50 cm · gray 0 · red +50 cm. Colors saturate at the endpoints. The layer covers only part of the study area.

record.label: NASA ARIA · NISAR line-of-sight displacement maps
record.finding: NASA ARIA used repeat-pass NISAR interferometry to document displacement after the June 24, 2026 earthquakes. The displayed reference is the June 18–30 line-of-sight pair.

limits: Sentinel-1 VV change measures brightness. NISAR phase-based displacement measures motion along the radar look direction. The terrain base is static elevation.
verification: Compare the displacement pattern with the other NISAR viewing geometries and independently reported shaking.
Use a later matched interferogram and ground measurements to check for postseismic movement.

outlook.summary: Prioritize repeat observations along the observed coastal deformation and consult official aftershock information for updates.
outlook.condition: Satellite radar cannot predict the timing, location or magnitude of the next earthquake.
